{{Short description|Canadian computer scientist}}
'''Georges Gonthier''' is a Canadian [[computer scientist]] and practitioner in [[Formal proof|formal mathematics]].  He led the formalization of the [[four color theorem]]<ref>{{cite book
 | last = Krantz | first = Steven G.
 | contribution = The Tantalizing Four-Color Theorem
 | doi = 10.1007/978-0-387-48744-1_6
 | isbn = 9780387487441
 | pages = 107–115
 | publisher = Springer New York
 | title = The Proof is in the Pudding
 | year = 2011}}</ref> and [[Feit–Thompson theorem|Feit–Thompson proof of the odd-order theorem]].<ref>[http://phys.org/news/2012-10-six-year-journey-proof-feit-thompson-theorem.html phys.org news article describing Feit-Thompson proof]</ref>  (Both were written using the [[proof assistant]] [[Rocq]].)

In 2011, as a principal researcher at Microsoft Research Cambridge, he received the EADS Foundation Grand Prize in Computer Science, given jointly by the European Aeronautic Defence and Space Company and the [[French Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/blog/gonthier-earns-eads-foundation-honor/|title= Gonthier Earns EADS Foundation Honor|date=November 22, 2011|work=Microsoft Research Blog|publisher=Microsoft|access-date=2024-06-11}}</ref>
